newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia police arrest youths after Lusaka clashes.
newsitem.headline: Zambia police arrest youths after Lusaka clashes.

text.p: Zambian police have arrested 13 youths after clashes between supporters of rival political parties in a township in the capital Lusaka on Monday, a spokesman said.

Police official Francis Musonda said supporters of former president Kenneth Kaunda's United National Independence Party (UNIP) and the ruling Movement for Multi-party Democracy (MMD) clashed in Lusaka's Chaisa township.
"The fight occurred when UNIP cadres attacked their MMD counterparts in an effort to evict them from the offices they said belonged to them," Musonda said.
Sixteen people were treated for injuries, he added.
The political climate in Zambia has heated up considerably ahead of general elections scheduled for November 18.
UNIP and six other parties are boycotting the polls in protest against new laws that prevent some candidates, including Kaunda, from standing for election.

The parties are campaigning for people to hand in their voters' cards to make sure they do not cast their ballots, but the government has threatened to arrest Kaunda if he does not call off the campaign, which it says is illegal.
